In the name of Allah, the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful.

Surah At-Takathur (The Abundance of Wealth)

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Abundance diverts you﴾ ﴿until you visit the graves.﴾

"Alhakum" means: it occupied you (shaghalakum). "Lahahu" means: it diverts him, i.e., it distracted him.

From this is the saying of Imru' al-Qays:

"So like you, pregnant, I have visited, and a nursing mother, and diverted her from the one with amulets, the weaned child."

That is: I occupied her.

"At-Takathur" means: mutual rivalry in abundance (al-mukathara). Here it is not mentioned in what the rivalry was, which diverted them.

Ibn al-Qayyim said: He left out its object either because the blameworthy thing is the very act of competing in abundance, not the thing one competes in, or to intend generality. End of quotation.

By the first, he (may Allah have mercy on him) means: the censure of anxiety (hala') and greed (naham).

By the second: so that it includes everything fit to be competed in: wealth, children, status, buildings, and plantations.

I have not found any of the exegetes mentioning a parallel to this verse.

However, they agreed in general on mentioning its occasion of revelation: that two clans boasted of their forefathers and the glories of their ancestors, so they counted the living, then went to the graves, and each of them counted what they had of the dead to boast of, competing with one another by counting them.

It was said: it concerns the Quraysh, between the Banu 'Abd Manaf and the Banu Sahm.

It was said: it concerns the Ansar.

It was said: it concerns the Jews and others, which indicates that the rivalry was in boasting of forefathers.

(p-77) Al-Qurtubi said: the verse includes all of what was mentioned and other things.

The context of the sound hadith is: "If the son of Adam had a valley of gold, he would love to have two valleys, and nothing will fill his mouth except dust, and Allah forgives whoever repents."

Thabit said, from Anas, from Ubayy: "We used to regard this as part of the Qur'an until there was revealed: ﴿Abundance diverts you﴾."

It seems that al-Qurtubi points by this to the fact that rivalry in wealth is also included.

Texts from the Book of Allah have come indicating that the rivalry which diverted them, and for which Allah censured them or warned them, is in all of these, as in His saying: ﴿Know that the life of this world is only play and amusement and adornment and boasting among yourselves and rivalry in wealth and children, like the example of rain whose vegetation pleases the disbelievers; then it dries up and you see it turned yellow; then it becomes debris﴾ up to His saying ﴿And the life of this world is not but the enjoyment of delusion﴾ [al-Hadid: 20].

In it is the explicit statement that the boasting and rivalry among them is in wealth and children.

Then other texts came with this meaning, such as His saying: ﴿And the life of this world is not but play and amusement, and the Hereafter is better for those who fear Allah﴾ [al-An'am: 32].

And His saying: ﴿And this worldly life is not but amusement and play, and indeed the home of the Hereafter is the [true] life, if they only knew﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 64].

And because the worldly life is in this position, the warning against it and the prohibition of being diverted by it came in His saying: ﴿O you who have believed, let not your wealth or your children divert you from the remembrance of Allah. And whoever does that, those are the losers﴾ [al-Munafiqun: 9].

And He made clear that what is with Allah is better for the believers than all of this, in His saying: ﴿And when they see a transaction or amusement, they disperse to it and leave you standing. Say: what is with Allah is better than amusement and than transaction, and Allah is the best of providers﴾ [al-Jumu'ah: 9].

What supports that the rivalry is in wealth and children within this same surah is what came at its end, (p-78) His saying: ﴿Then you will be asked that Day about the pleasure﴾ [at-Takathur: 8], for its correspondence to the beginning of the surah,

as is evident from the inclusion of pleasure initially covering wealth.

And His saying: ﴿until you visit the graves.﴾

From it, those who said that their boasting drove them to go to the graves in order to compete with their dead took this, as came in the reports on the occasions of revelation mentioned earlier.

The correct view regarding "you visit the graves" is: it means you died, because the dead person comes to the grave like a visitor, since his presence in it is temporary.

It has been related that a Bedouin heard this verse and said: "They were resurrected, by the Lord of the Ka'bah!" He was asked about that, and he said: "Because a visitor must depart."

* *

A Note

Some scholars discussed the matter of visiting graves here, based on the hadith: "I had forbidden you from visiting graves; now visit them, for they make one detached from the world and remind of the Hereafter."

They said: the prohibition was general because of mentioning the glories of forefathers and the dead; then after that, visiting was permitted, and they differed about who was permitted. It was said: for men but not women, since women are not included in the plural "you" in "visit them" (fazuruha). It was said: it is general to men and women. Each side cited evidences whose presentation would be lengthy.

However, in summary, to clarify the stronger view, we give a portion of the discussion.

Those who prohibited it for women said: they remain under the original prohibition, and the permission did not include them, and the curse came upon women who visit.

Those who permitted it said: they enter implicitly in the address to men, as they enter in such a saying as: ﴿And establish prayer and give zakah﴾ [al-Baqarah: 43], for they definitely enter.

They also said: the curse mentioned came in the hadith in two narrations: the narration "Allah curses the women who visit graves," and what came: "Allah curses the women who frequently visit graves and those who take lamps over them," to the end.

(p-79) According to the intensive form, "zawwarat" (frequent visitors) does not include mere visiting, but applies specifically to those who do so excessively, because by excess they are not safe from the customs of the Jahiliyyah, namely enumerating the glories of the dead, which is forbidden in the original verse.

As for mere visiting without excess or lingering, it is not included.

They cited for this the hadith of 'A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her, when she mentioned to him ﷺ the greeting upon the people of al-Baqi', and she said: "What should I say, O Messenger of Allah, if I visit the graves? He said: Say: Peace be upon you, O abode of believing people," the hadith.

He ﷺ approved of her, on the basis that she visits graves, and taught her what to say if she visits.

Likewise, "the story of his passing by a woman weeping at a grave, and he spoke to her, and she said: 'Go away from me,' not knowing who he was; when he left her, she was told: 'It is the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.' She came apologizing, and he said to her: 'Patience is only at the first shock.'"

He did not mention to her the prohibition of visiting graves, even though he saw her weeping.

These are explicit evidences for permitting visitation. In terms of meaning, the benefit of visitation is equally needed by men, namely that visiting graves makes one detached from the world and inclined toward the Hereafter.

This is not specific to men without women; rather women may be even more in need of it than men.

In any case, the stronger view from these texts, and Allah knows best, is permissibility for those who do not do so excessively and do not say what is unseemly, which was the cause of the first prohibition. And knowledge is with Allah.

* *

Another Note

Among the subtle points in the exegesis is what Abu Hayyan mentioned concerning the rivalry in His saying: ﴿until you visit the graves﴾, the text of which is:

It was said: this is a rebuke for excess in visiting, multiplying by those who passed and praising their memory. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ had forbidden visiting graves, then said: "visit them," an permission for taking admonition from them, not for the sense of vainglory and boasting.

Then he said: Ibn 'Atiyyah said: as people do in lingering at them, decorating them with stone and marble, coloring them for status, and placing nawawis (lamps, i.e., fanus, which are lamps) upon them.

Then Abu Hayyan and Ibn 'Atiyyah said: he saw only the graves of the people of al-Andalus. How then if he saw what the people of Egypt boast of in their burial grounds at al-Qarafa al-Kubra, al-Qarafa al-Sughra, Bab al-Nasr and other places, and what wealth is wasted in them; he would be astonished at that and would see what had not entered the mind.

As for boasting in visiting: among those who attribute themselves to Sufism there are groups who have no occupation except visiting graves: "I visited the tomb of my master so-and-so in such-and-such place, the tomb of so-and-so in such-and-such place, and Shaykh so-and-so in such-and-such place," and they mention regions they have traversed on foot in asceticism.

They have memorized stories about the people of those graves and those shaykhs, enough that if they were written down they would fill volumes. Yet they do not know the obligatory acts of ablution nor its sunnahs.

Kings and common people have been made subservient to them in thinking well of them and spending wealth on them. As for whoever among them deviates by speaking to the common folk and bringing wonders, they say: "This is an opening of knowledge of the divine kind (al-'ilm al-ladunni) granted by al-Khidr."

To the point that whoever claims knowledge, when he sees the popularity of this group, follows their path, transmits many of their stories, and mixes that with a little knowledge, seeking wealth, status, and kissing of hands.

We ask Allah, Mighty and Majestic, to grant us success in obeying Him. End of quotation, verbatim.

What he (may Allah have mercy on him) said is among the greatest things by which Muslims have been afflicted in both their religion and their worldly affairs together.

As for their religion: it is the excess that he ﷺ forbade, to safeguard tawhid from asking other than Allah.

As for worldly affairs: many of these people abandon the interests of their worldly life, whether farming, trade, or crafts, and wander around those places, neglecting and wasting those whose striving is better than voluntary acts of worship.

It is incumbent upon students of knowledge in every place and time to guide the ignorant among them, and to make clear to the people in general the error and ignorance of those, and that journeying to those graves is not from the Sunnah of the Messenger, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him, nor was it the practice of the rightly guided caliphs, nor of the general body of the Companions and the Successors, nor of the imams of the four schools, may Allah have mercy on them all.

Rather, the practice of all of them was visiting the graves nearby to give them greetings of peace, to pray for them, to take admonition from their state, and to prepare for what they have gone to.

We ask Allah for guidance and success in following the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and in emulating the footsteps of the earlier generations of this Ummah. Ameen.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 102, verse 3:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Nay, you will come to know﴾ ﴿Then, nay, you will come to know﴾.

"Nay" (kalla): a rebuke against the preoccupation (al-talahhi) and the mutual rivalry in increase (al-takathur) mentioned. "You will come to know" (sawfa ta'lamun): that is, the reality of the matter (haqiqat al-amr) and the outcome (maghabbat) of this preoccupation. ﴿Then, nay, you will come to know﴾ is a repetition for emphasis (ta'kid).

It has also been said that there is no repetition, on the basis of what has been related from ʿAli, may Allah be pleased with him: that the first is in the grave and the second is on the Day of Resurrection. And this is a reasonable view (ma'qul).

Some scholars have used this as evidence for the punishment of the grave ('adhab al-qabr).

The authenticity of the hadith concerning the grave is well known: "The grave is either a garden from the gardens of Paradise, or a pit from the pits of the Fire."

The questioning in it is well known, but they meant its source (ma'khadhahu) from the Qur'an.

Our Shaykh, may Allah's mercy be upon him and upon us, had previously, in the discussion of Surah Ghafir, at: ﴿And there surrounded the people of Pharaoh the worst of punishment﴾ [Ghafir: 45], established the punishment of the grave from the Qur'an.

Likewise, its meaning was explained at the end of Surah al-Zukhruf in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So turn away from them and say, "Peace." But they will come to know﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 89].

This rebuke and warning here is a response to what they were upon in rivalry in increase, as the poet said:

"You are not, among them, the most in number of pebbles, but honour belongs only to the one who increases [his tally]."

The clearest evidence from the Qur'an for establishing the punishment of the grave is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿The Fire, they are exposed to it morning and evening; and on the Day the Hour is established, "Admit the people of Pharaoh to the severest punishment."﴾ Because the first is in this world, and the second is in the Hereafter.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 102, verse 5:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Nay, were you to know with the knowledge of certainty﴾ ﴿you would surely see the Blazing Fire﴾ ﴿and then you would surely see it with the eye of certainty﴾.

"Law" (لَوْ): here it is conditional (شَرْطِيَّة), and its answer (جَوابُها) is omitted by agreement. Ibn Kathir estimated it as: "Were you to know it with the true knowledge, the abundance (of worldly gain) would not have distracted you from seeking the Hereafter, until you went to the graveyards." As for "the knowledge of certainty" (عِلْمُ اليَقِينِ): Abu Hayyan permitted the annexation of a thing to itself (إضافَةُ الشَّيْءِ لِنَفْسِهِ), meaning for the difference in description, since knowledge is certainty, but it is more emphatic than it.

And from Hassan, his saying:

Hassan's verse:
"We marched, and they marched to Badr for their own destruction; had they known the certainty of knowledge, they would not have marched."

As for ﴿you would surely see the Blazing Fire﴾: it is the answer to an omitted oath (لِقَسَمٍ مَحْذُوفٍ).

He said: the intended seeing of it is at the first of the Resurrection, or at the time of passing over it (الوُرُود), or at the time when the state is uncovered in the grave.

As for ﴿and then you would surely see it with the eye of certainty﴾: it has been said that this is for the disbeliever upon his entering it; this is the summary of the words of the exegetes.

It is known that this is not merely an informing of seeing it, but a severe threat and a warning with it; because mere seeing is known: ﴿And there is none of you but will pass over it﴾ [Maryam: 71], but this seeing is more specific, as in His saying: ﴿And the criminals will see the Fire and will assume that they are going to fall into it﴾ [al-Kahf: 53], meaning they became certain, by the evidence of His saying: ﴿and they will not find from it any escape﴾ [al-Kahf: 53].

A point may appear in this context, which is that the seeing here of the Fire is of two kinds:

The first seeing: the seeing of knowledge and certainty, in His saying: ﴿were you to know with the knowledge of certainty﴾, a knowledge by which you would be certain of the reality of the Day of Resurrection; you would be as one who witnesses its terrors and observes its conditions, as in the Hadith of Ihsan: "that you worship Allah as if you see Him."

And a similar thing occurred in the story of al-Siddiq when he was informed of the news of the Isra' (Night Journey), and he said: "Muhammad has spoken the truth." They said: "Do you affirm him while you did not hear it from him?" He said: "Indeed I affirm him regarding more than that."

So, because of his knowledge with the knowledge of certainty of his truthfulness ﷺ in what he reports, he affirmed the Isra' as if he were seeing it.

The second seeing is the seeing of the eye and of witnessing, so it is the eye of certainty.

We have already mentioned the three degrees of knowledge: the knowledge of certainty (عِلْمُ اليَقِينِ), the eye of certainty (عَيْنُ اليَقِينِ), and the truth of certainty (حَقُّ اليَقِينِ).

So knowledge (العِلْم) is what comes from evidences.

The eye of certainty (عَيْنُ اليَقِينِ) is what comes from direct witnessing.

The truth of certainty (حَقُّ اليَقِينِ) is what comes from immersion and close contact, as knowledge of the Ka'bah and its direction is the knowledge of certainty; when one sees it, it is the eye of certainty regarding its existence; when one enters it and is inside it, it is the truth of certainty regarding its existence. And Allah knows best.

**Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Then you will surely be questioned that Day about the bounties.﴾**

The root meaning of *al-na'im* (bounty, blessing) is every state of ease and comfort, derived from *al-nu'umah* and *al-layyunah*, which are the opposite of roughness, dryness, and hardship. This is indicated by His saying: ﴿And whatever bounty you have is from Allah﴾ [An-Nahl: 53].

Then He said: ﴿When adversity touches you, to Him you cry for help﴾ [An-Nahl: 53], contrasting bounty with adversity.

Similarly, His saying: ﴿And if We let him taste a bounty after hardship has touched him, he will surely say, "The evils have gone from me"﴾ [Hud: 10].

On this basis, the bounties of Allah are countless, as He said: ﴿And if you tried to count the bounties of Allah, you could not enumerate them﴾ [An-Nahl: 18].

From this you will know that everything the *mufassirun* (Qur'anic exegetes) have said is by way of example, not restriction, as Allah said: ﴿you could not enumerate them﴾.

The foundations of these bounties, the first of them, is Islam: ﴿Today I have perfected for you your religion, completed My favour upon you, and approved for you Islam as a religion﴾ [Al-Ma'idah: 3].

Included in them are the bounties of legislation and of relief from what was imposed on the earlier nations.

(p-84) Also included is the bounty of brotherhood in Allah: ﴿And remember the favour of Allah upon you when you were enemies and He brought your hearts together, and you became, by His favour, brothers﴾ [Al 'Imran: 103], and much else besides.

The second: health, soundness of creation, and well-being. Among the perfection of creation are the senses: ﴿Did We not make for him two eyes?﴾ ﴿and a tongue and two lips?﴾ [Al-Balad: 8–9].

Then He said: ﴿Indeed, the hearing, the sight, and the heart — each of those will be questioned﴾ [Al-Isra': 36].

The third: wealth, whether in its acquisition or its spending. In its acquisition from what is lawful there is a bounty, and in its spending in its proper channels there is a bounty.

These are the foundations of the bounties. So what is one questioned about? The *Sunnah* (the Prophetic tradition) has informed us that one will be questioned about all of that, in general and in detail.

As for religion, wealth, and health, the summary of the hadith states: "When the Day of Resurrection comes, the foot of a servant will not move until he is questioned about five things: about his life, how he spent it; about his knowledge, what he did with it; about his wealth, from where he earned it and how he spent it; and about his youth, how he consumed it."

Because of the greatness and comprehensiveness of this verse, it has become a text cited as an example, for the Sunnah has detailed particulars that the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had not thought of.

Al-Qurtubi quoted what is recorded in Sahih Muslim from Abu Hurairah (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out one day or night, and found Abu Bakr and 'Umar. He said, 'What brought you out of your houses at this hour?' They said, 'Hunger, O Messenger of Allah!' He said, 'And I too — by the One in whose hand is my soul, what brought you out has brought me out. Stand up.' So they stood with him and came to a man of the Ansar, but he was not in his house. When his wife saw him, she said, 'Welcome, and well come!' The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to her, 'Where is so-and-so?' She said, 'He has gone to fetch us sweet water,' meaning he has gone to seek sweet water. Then the Ansari came, looked at the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and his two companions, and said, 'Praise be to Allah, there is no one today more honourable in hospitality than I.' He went and brought them a cluster of dates containing unripe, half-ripe, and ripe dates, and said, 'Eat from these.' He took a knife, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, 'Beware of the milch animal.' So he slaughtered for them. They ate from the sheep and from that cluster, and drank. (p-85) When they were full and satisfied, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to Abu Bakr and 'Umar: 'By the One in whose hand is my soul, you will surely be questioned on the Day of Resurrection about this bounty: hunger drove you out of your houses, and you did not return until this bounty reached you.'" At-Tirmidhi also recorded it.

In his version he said: "This, by the One in whose hand is my soul, is of the bounty about which you will be questioned on the Day of Resurrection: cool shade, fresh and pleasant, and cold water."

He gave the Ansari man a kunyah, saying: Abu al-Haytham ibn al-Tayyihan.

Al-Qurtubi said: I say, the name of this man is Malik ibn al-Tayyihan, and he is called Abu al-Haytham.

Ibn Kathir also mentioned this story through several chains.

Among them, in Ahmad's collection: "'Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) took a *faraq* and struck it on the ground, and said, 'O Messenger of Allah, are we really going to be questioned about this?' He said, 'Yes, except for three things: a piece of cloth with which a man covers his private parts, a morsel with which he stills his hunger, or a shelter that shields him from heat and cold.'"

Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah said: What fills hunger and covers the private parts of coarse food is not something a person will be questioned about on the Day of Resurrection; rather he will be questioned about bounty. The evidence for this is that Allah settled Adam in Paradise and said to him: ﴿Indeed, it is yours that you will not hunger therein or go naked﴾ ﴿and that you will not thirst therein or be exposed to the sun﴾ [Ta-Ha: 118–119].

These four things, which fill hunger, quench thirst, shelter from heat, and cover the private parts, were absolutely available to Adam (peace be upon him), with no reckoning for him concerning them, because he could not do without them.

It is also reported from Ahmad, with his chain: "They were sitting when the Prophet ﷺ came upon them, and there was a trace of water on his head. We said, 'O Messenger of Allah, we see you in good spirits?' He said, 'Indeed.' He said: The people had been discussing wealth, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'There is no harm in wealth for one who fears Allah, and health for one who fears Allah is better than wealth, and contentment of soul is among the bounties.'"

He said: Ibn Majah also narrated it from Abu Hurairah.

On this basis, it is established from the Book and the Sunnah that the bounty which is the subject of questioning on the Day of Resurrection (p-86) is general, covering everything a person enjoys in this world, whether sensory or immaterial.

To the point that they said: sleep along with good health. They also said: the questioning is general, for both the disbeliever and the believer. For the disbeliever it is reproach, rebuke, and reckoning; for the believer it is confirmation, according to his gratitude for the bounty or his denial of it, and the manner in which he disposed of it. And Allah knows best.

All of this is intended to urge gratitude for the bounty, acknowledgment of the Benefactor, and fulfilment of His right in it, glory be to Him, as Allah the Exalted said concerning the Prophet of Allah: ﴿My Lord, enable me to be grateful for Your favour which You have bestowed upon me and upon my parents, and to do righteousness that You will accept, and make righteous for me my offspring. Indeed, I have repented to You, and indeed, I am of the Muslims﴾ [Al-Ahqaf: 15].

O Allah, enable us to be grateful for Your bounty, and make what You have bestowed upon us a help to us in obeying You.
